notes: Facility-row quote caveat: the Caterpillar 2024 row carries the $725M total from the article headline (Inside Indiana Business, 2024-02-23) and its $625M machinery/equipment/rail plus $100M construction split. The quoted sentence is the square-footage sentence because the total is not in one verbatim sentence I could quote. Verify the headline wording before relying on the total.

Caterpillar Lafayette: the 2024 article says the expansion is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with equipment installed in 2027. The Aug 2026 Manufacturing Today article ties the $890M plan to retention of 1,995 employees (not new jobs) and reports the Lafayette Redevelopment Commission had abatement resolutions scheduled for Aug 27, 2026 with no outcome given. Cited Caterpillar Oct 2025 release and 10-year $100M abatement report were search snippets, not opened pages.

Mitsubishi Power Savannah Machinery Works: the AJC article says the plant has the capacity to manufacture a dozen turbines annually and that the expansion is expected to double production capacity. It also says no opening date has been set (The company did not divulge an opening date target). The 450,000 sq ft is an added building area, not acreage. The Pooler, GA location and the 2010 opening date came from search snippets, not an opened page.

Siemens Energy NC: the Feb 2026 release gives $1 billion as the national investment and 500 jobs across the three NC communities, with no per-site split. The NC investment total of $421M (NC Capital Group) and the Charlotte restart after a six-year pause (charlottenc.gov) are search-snippet figures; the city page was blocked (Akamai) on fetch. The release names Winston-Salem for gas turbine parts; a second source also names Rural Hall, which I did not open. Raleigh is grid technology, not manufacturing.

GE Vernova: the investing-in-manufacturing page is undated (links point to Jan 2025; footer 2026) and uses 2025-26 job windows. Its table lists Richmond VA at $17M and 25 jobs, Chamblee GA at $2M, Bangor ME at $22M and 50 jobs (text says more than $20M), and Parsippany NJ with no jobs. The Richmond and Chamblee dollar figures and the Bangor job count are table values that the quoted sentences do not contain, so those fields are null or unquoted. The page's Niskayuna and Wilmington NC entries are research or nuclear and are excluded. Wind sites (Pensacola, Grand Forks, Amarillo, Schenectady wind) are excluded as not gas or steam turbine. GE Vernova also reports Charleroi PA and Pittsburgh PA grid and power-conversion sites, excluded as off-scope.

GE Vernova Greenville: the press release says the plant has produced gas turbines since 1968. Search snippets (not opened) give a 70 to 80 heavy-duty turbines per year target from the second half of 2026, the Woodward Greenville combustion-parts site acquisition (April 2025), and a 1.55M sq ft footprint from SC Daily Gazette (that page returned HTTP 403). GE Schenectady $41M and 50-job steam and generator Center of Excellence (Aug 2025) comes from search snippets of the Governor's and ESD releases, not opened pages.

Solar Turbines: Wamego, KS is a takeover of a closed Caterpillar Work Tools plant; Caterpillar announced the closure in June 2024. The first Wamego turbine shipped January 2026, and about 220 existing employees moved into the operation (transitioned staff, not new hires). Investment and square footage are not stated. No new San Diego expansion was found; the San Diego production claim (250th Titan 250) and the employee count (7,475 LinkedIn vs 9,000 PitchBook) are unverified snippets.

Howmet: the IndustrialInfo article's Morristown TN ceramic-core expansion (started Q2 2025) has no verbatim sentence I could quote, so it is listed here, not as a facility row. The article gives Howmet 37 US facilities, a CEO quote 'This growing level of demand continues into the 2030s', and Q3 gas-turbine revenue up 45%. Wichita Falls is the only Howmet row with a city-council-approved economic development package ($5.275M, approved in September, year not stated); that package is not counted as investment. The article's date is not stated, so published is null.

Not found as quotable US plant expansions: Doosan Enerbility (gas turbines built in Changwon, Korea; a 380 MW unit shipped to a US project; Doosan says it has contracted 12 US gas turbines with one per month from May 2029, from a search snippet; no US factory found; Houston is a service subsidiary). Wartsila (429 MW US data-center engine order and a 282 MW Ohio order, both project orders, not plant expansions). Cummins ($450M gas and diesel generator-set expansion, single secondary source, plant location not given). Doncasters and PCC (no confirmed US plant expansion in results). Boom Supersonic (aircraft turbine superfactory, not stationary gas turbines; excluded).

Requirements gap, natural gas and power for test stands: no opened source gives a factory's natural-gas supply or power demand. The only test-cell sources found were the EthosEnergy testing page (fetch returned HTTP 503), a 2011 GE Greenville full-speed full-load test facility in a New York PSC filing (not opened), and a blog claiming factory test cells cannot absorb 400+ MW (not opened). Treat the natural-gas and power factors as unverified until the EthosEnergy page or an OEM test-facility source can be opened.

Transport detail for the requirements: the Barnhart page describes a steam turbine moved from the Port of Houston by floating crane onto a hopper barge to the Port of Catoosa, OK, with a Goldhofer trailer and rail-car loading; the gas turbine came from Savannah by barge. Its origin site and weights are not stated, and the project date is not given. The Savannah origin matches the Mitsubishi Savannah Machinery Works facility, but the page does not name the manufacturer.

Not opened, lead only: a USPTO gas-turbine half-casing patent describes many power-plant sites lacking crane capacity and transport lanes that can carry a fully assembled turbine. Use for a heavy-haul requirement only after the patent page is opened and quoted.

Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi job figures are announced totals and may not match what each plant ends up hiring. Caterpillar, Mitsubishi and Siemens dates are announcement dates, not construction or production dates.
